hook.reason: The title line "Sun lights half, the Moon goes round" is short, concrete and close to the core idea, and it opens and closes the chorus. But it names the cause rather than the big move of the shape changing, and "the Moon goes round" is somewhat loose. The lesson opens on a real question ("If the Moon is a round ball, why does it look like a thin sliver..."), and the narration opens on the thin Moon after sunset, which is in the learner's world.

frame.reason: The lamp, ball and head model is an apt picture of the whole mechanism, and it appears in the lesson, narration and verse 1. But it is dropped from the chorus, bridge and outro after verse 1, so the song does not carry it through. The day-and-night aside is a second picture but it is a short link, not a rival. The eclipse bridge also pulls the song away from the frame.

why_chain.reason: The lesson lists all five links with their causes ("so its place around Earth keeps changing", "so we see a different phase"). The narration follows in order, but link 4 is only shown through waxing and waning, and link 5 is stated with little reasoning ("the same order repeats"). Narration also runs long on eclipses after the chain ends. The song carries the gist, but a good share of verse 2 and the whole bridge drift to eclipse content.

key_lines.reason: Most lines are steps, such as "Sun lights the facing side → half the Moon always lit" and "Moon orbits Earth → its place keeps changing". But the first is a bare question label, "Lamp = Sun, ball = Moon, your head = Earth" is a label, and the waxing and waning lines are terms rather than steps in the chain. The last line is about eclipses and there is no closing core idea line. The key line for the lamp model starts at v1-1, which is a fair match. Link 4 (a different amount of lit half faces Earth) is only implied.

errors: "At new moon, the side we never see is lit" / "Our side's all dark" is fine; but the song line "Sun lights half, the Moon goes round" and the narration "n2: Over the next nights it grows into half a circle, and about a week later it's full" is imprecise: the crescent grows to first quarter in about a week, but full moon comes about two weeks after new moon, and a thin crescent a few days after new moon is not a week before full. Correction: from a thin crescent, full moon is about 10 to 12 days away.

"n6/n7" lamp model: turning in a circle in place makes the observer, not the ball, move, so the ball stays in the same place; this works as a model but the ball is held still while you turn, so it is the viewer's head that is Earth, which is correct. No error here, but "Hold the ball at arm's length and turn" does not show the Moon orbiting; it is a fair simplification.
"The same side of the Moon always faces Earth, because the Moon spins once on its axis each time it goes around Earth" is in the facts but the lesson avoids it; no error in the lesson.

The lesson says phases repeat about every 29.5 days, while the Moon orbits Earth "about once a month"; the 27.3-day orbit versus 29.5-day phase cycle is blurred, so "the Moon takes the same path every orbit, so the phases repeat" is a mild imprecision.

accuracy.reason: The core claims are right: half is lit, new moon has the Moon between Earth and Sun, the far side is lit at new moon, and Earth's shadow only matters at lunar eclipse at full moon. The imprecision is "Over the next nights it grows into half a circle, and about a week later it's full" (n2), where full moon is closer to two weeks after new moon and a week after first quarter. The 27.3-day orbit versus 29.5-day phase cycle is blurred as well. A teacher would tighten these, but nothing seriously wrong would be carried away.

singability.reason: Many lines are natural and whole, such as "Hold a ball by a lamp and turn around slow" and the chant-like "Sun lights half, the Moon goes round". The rhymes are mostly clean. But several lines run long and read like captions: "Back to new in about twenty-nine and a half days" and "So the cycle repeats in the same order, phase by phase" (the latter rhymes with "days" only by a weak tag). The bridge lines such as "Earth blocks the sunlight from the Moon's bright face" are textbook sentences, and "Sun, Earth, Moon in line on a full moon night" is crowded. The chorus is a good chant, though it carries "waxing" and "waning" as terms.

lesson_clarity.reason: It opens on a question, builds the model, lists the five steps with causes, and asks a predict question ("So what do you think we see when the Moon is on the far side of Earth from the Sun?") answered right after. It names the misconception and explains why it is wrong. The check, "why can't we see the Moon at all at new moon?", is answerable by someone who understood. But it adds many terms (waxing, waning, crescent, gibbous, quarters) and a lunar eclipse and orbit tilt tangent that a first-time 11-year-old does not need, and the five steps read a little like a list.
